# brig sandbox create

Create an OpenShell sandbox in a VM, with host directories mounted read-only

## Synopsis

```text
brig sandbox create [NAME] [-w W] [--mount DIR:TARGET]... [--connect] [-- OPENSHELL-ARGS...]
```

## Description

Run openshell sandbox create against VM NAME's gateway, with each
--mount DIR:TARGET showing host directory DIR read-only at TARGET in the
sandbox. Arguments after -- go to openshell sandbox create as they are.
Without NAME, the VM is the one that [`brig use`](brig-use.md) selected.

The sandbox is created in workspace W of the gateway (-w), by default the one
that $BRIG\_WORKSPACE names, else default. --mount works only in workspace
default.

A sandbox sees DIR through a read-only sandbox mount of the VM (see [`brig create`](brig-create.md) --help). brig uses the VM's sandbox mount of DIR, or adds one to the
running VM, at /mnt/\<tag\> in the VM, which stays until [`brig update`](brig-update.md)
--remove-mount removes it. As [`brig env`](brig-env.md) does, it points openshell at the VM's
default sandbox policy, if it has one.

The sandbox gets the providers that --provider names after --, and no
others: as [`brig ui`](brig-ui.md) does, brig passes --no-auto-providers, so that a provider
the gateway lacks is an error rather than one that openshell creates from
credentials it finds on the host. Give --auto-providers after -- for
openshell's own behaviour.

With --connect, brig starts the VM first if it is stopped, as [`brig start`](brig-start.md)
--wait does, creates the sandbox without attaching to it, waits until it is
ready and then connects this terminal to it, as [`brig sandbox connect`](brig-sandbox-connect.md) does.
It needs the sandbox's --name after --.

## Examples

```sh
brig sandbox create dev --mount ~/src/pi-kit:/usr/local/share/pi-kit -- \
  --name kit-dev --from localhost/pi-agent:2026-10-08 --provider llm
brig use dev && brig sandbox create -m ~/notes:/usr/local/share/notes
brig sandbox create dev --connect -m ~/src/webapp:/sandbox/src -- --name webapp --template pi
```

## Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--connect` | start the VM if needed, wait until the sandbox is ready and connect to it |
| `-m, --mount stringArray` | show host directory DIR read-only at TARGET in the sandbox: DIR:TARGET (repeatable) |
| `-w, --workspace string` | the workspace of the gateway to work in (default: $BRIG\_WORKSPACE, else default) |

The [global options](brig.md#options) of brig apply too.
